spec.description: SIPI IIIF media server, driven by SIPI's OpenTelemetry (OTLP) metrics (service_name=sipi). Latency, throughput, caching, decode-memory and pool saturation, rate limiting, errors, plus the dsp-api /admin/files permission route SIPI calls on every request. The legacy Prometheus scrape (service DSP_iiif_iiif) is intentionally excluded.

spec.title: Environment
spec.description: Ansible host (OTLP resource attribute deployment.environment.name) the dashboard is reading: the primary VRE box vre-$environment-01. SIPI also runs on LS/RDU hosts; all panels here are scoped to this host only.

spec.title: SIPI Version
spec.description: service.version from the OTLP resource (attached to all spans and metrics), most recently reported by the primary VRE host.

spec.title: Request Rate
spec.description: HTTP requests per second served by SIPI (OTLP http.server.request.duration count), all routes, primary VRE host.

spec.title: P95 Latency
spec.description: 95th-percentile HTTP request latency across all SIPI routes (OTLP http.server.request.duration), primary VRE host.

spec.title: Cache Hit Ratio
spec.description: Share of serves answered from the file-based image cache: hits / (hits + misses). A falling ratio means more full decodes, i.e. higher CPU and latency.

spec.title: 5xx Rate
spec.description: Server-error responses per second (HTTP 5xx), all SIPI routes, primary VRE host.

spec.title: Latency Percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
spec.description: p50/p95/p99 HTTP request latency across all SIPI routes (OTLP http.server.request.duration histogram), primary VRE host.

spec.title: Auth route request rate by status (/admin/files)
spec.description: dsp-api permission check SIPI calls on every IIIF request (tapir_request_duration_seconds, scoped by instance to the primary VRE host). 4xx = auth denials, 5xx = errors.

spec.title: Auth route avg latency (/admin/files)
spec.description: Average latency of the dsp-api permission check (rate of sum / rate of count; the tapir metric has no histogram buckets, so no percentiles). Adds directly to every IIIF request.

spec.title: Cache Usage vs Limit
spec.description: Bytes in the file-based image cache vs the configured size limit (sipi.cache.size_bytes / size_limit_bytes). LRU eviction starts when a limit is reached; an unlimited cache (-1) hides the limit series.

spec.title: Cache Files vs Limit
spec.description: Files in the image cache vs the configured file-count limit. Dual-limit LRU: eviction triggers on size or file count, whichever is hit first.

spec.title: Cache Evictions & Skips (rate)
spec.description: Cache maintenance per second: entries evicted by the LRU, and writes skipped because the file was too large to cache.

spec.title: Preflight Cache Hit Ratio
spec.description: Share of preflight authorization decisions served from the in-shell access cache (a hit skips the Lua preflight hook entirely).

spec.title: Decode Memory Used vs Budget
spec.description: Decode-memory admission control: bytes currently reserved by in-flight decodes vs the configured budget. Decodes whose estimate would exceed the budget are rejected. The gauge is sampled at export interval, so short spikes between exports are not visible.

spec.title: Decode Memory Admission (rate)
spec.description: Admission-control decisions on the decode-memory budget: acquired = admitted; rejected = would exceed the budget; near_limit = usage crossed 80% of budget; shadow_rejected = would have been rejected while the budget runs in non-enforcing shadow mode.

spec.title: Worker Pool Permits (in use vs total)
spec.description: Engine worker-pool permits held vs total (SIPI_NTHREADS). In use = total means every worker is busy and new requests queue.

spec.title: Worker Pool Waiting
spec.description: Requests queued waiting for a worker permit. Sustained non-zero means the pool is saturated; see load-shed/timeout for the overflow.

spec.title: Pool Load-Shed & Queue Timeout (rate)
spec.description: Overload signals per second: requests shed with 503 because the queue was full, and requests that timed out waiting for a permit.

spec.title: Rate Limit: Allowed vs Rejected (rate)
spec.description: Per-client rate limiter: requests allowed vs rejected, per second.

spec.title: Rate Limit: Near-Limit & Shadow-Rejected (rate)
spec.description: Rate-limiter early warnings per second: near_limit = a client crossed 80% of its budget; shadow_rejected = would have been rejected while the limiter runs in non-enforcing shadow mode.

spec.title: Rate Limit: Clients Tracked
spec.description: Active client entries in the rate limiter (distinct clients seen within the tracking window).

spec.title: Errors (rate)
spec.description: Engine error signals per second: requests rejected by the output pixel limit (image too large), allocation failures during image processing, and requests aborted by client disconnect.

spec.title: SIPI Container CPU Usage
spec.description: cAdvisor CPU usage of the SIPI container (service DSP_iiif_iiif) on the primary VRE host, in cores.

spec.title: SIPI Container Memory Usage
spec.description: cAdvisor container metrics for the SIPI container (service DSP_iiif_iiif) on the primary VRE host. 'working set' is the real, non-reclaimable memory the cgroup OOM killer acts on; 'usage (incl. page cache)' additionally counts reclaimable page cache from reading image files, so it saturates at the limit under load without indicating a problem. 'limit' is the container memory limit - working set approaching it risks an OOM kill. On images before SIPI 6.2.3 the working set ratchets up to a concurrency x peak-decode watermark and plateaus (glibc malloc arenas retain freed decode buffers); that is expected, not a leak.

options.content: The panels below query SIPI instruments that currently return **no series over OTLP** (`service_name="sipi"`). Either the instrument is not bridged from the C++ engine to the Rust OTLP path, or it only emits under specific conditions (e.g. non-zero decode estimates). Use this row to spot gaps and decide what still needs to be bridged. If a panel here starts showing data, move it into the relevant section above.

spec.title: Decode Memory Estimate (p95)
spec.description: p95 of the per-request estimated decode memory (sipi_decode_memory_estimate_bytes). Feeds the decode-memory budget admission control that rate-limits heavy requests.

spec.title: Rejected Connections (rate)
spec.description: sipi_rejected_connections_total. Not bridged to OTLP (always zero on the FFI serve path). Use Pool Waiting / Load-Shed instead.

spec.title: Waiting Connections
spec.description: sipi_waiting_connections. Not bridged to OTLP. Use sipi.pool.waiting instead.

spec.title: Rate Limit Decisions by action (rate)
spec.description: sipi_rate_limit_decisions_total{action}. Legacy single-family counter; the OTLP path splits this into allowed / rejected / near_limit / shadow_rejected instead.

spec.title: Essentials Hash Mismatch (rate)
spec.description: sipi_essentials_hash_mismatch_total. Not bridged to OTLP today (C++/Prometheus-only integrity tripwire).

spec.title: Read-shape Fast Path (rate)
spec.description: sipi_read_shape_fast_path_total{format,outcome}. Not bridged to OTLP today (C++/Prometheus-only).

spec.title: Allocator: In Use vs Retained
spec.description: Process-allocator accounting (sipi_malloc_* gauges, SIPI > 6.2.3; empty until that release is deployed). In use = allocated and not yet freed — grows without bound only under a true leak. Retained = freed but held by the allocator instead of returned to the OS — the series that explains an RSS ratchet with no leak (the 2026-07-29 OOM). See sipi docs/adr/0019-mimalloc-production-allocator.md.

spec.title: Allocator: Held from OS
spec.description: Bytes the allocator holds from the OS backing RSS (arena) and the mmap-served share outside the regular heap (sipi_malloc_* gauges, SIPI > 6.2.3). The gap between Held-from-OS and the Resources row's container working set is non-allocator memory (thread stacks, code, page tables).
